taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-24, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1101.7 | 4.18 | 4.18
2 | 1144.4 | 12.44 | 16.62
3 | 549.8 | 0.62 | 17.24
4 | 173.3 | 7.65 | 24.89
5 | 2079.8 | 25.05 | 49.94
6 | 1111.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KQHK-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine if the label "KQHK-type" is correct, we evaluate the resistivity changes for each group of three consecutive layers:

1.  **Layers 1, 2, 3:** Resistivities are 1101.7, 1144.4, and 549.8. Since $1101.7 < 1144.4 > 549.8$, this matches the **K** pattern ($\rho_1 < \rho_2 > \rho_3$).
2.  **Layers 2, 3, 4:** Resistivities are 1144.4, 549.8, and 173.3. Since $1144.4 > 549.8 > 173.3$, this matches the **Q** pattern ($\rho_2 > \rho_3 > \rho_4$).
3.  **Layers 3, 4, 5:** Resistivities are 549.8, 173.3, and 2079.8. Since $549.8 > 173.3 < 2079.8$, this matches the **H** pattern ($\rho_3 > \rho_4 < \rho_5$).
4.  **Layers 4, 5, 6:** Resistivities are 173.3, 2079.8, and 1111.4. Since $173.3 < 2079.8 > 1111.4$, this matches the **K** pattern ($\rho_4 < \rho_5 > \rho_6$).

Combining these letters in depth order gives **KQHK**.

{"label_correct": true, "curve_type": "KQHK"}
